transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Hello, please share your thoughts on what democracy means to you personally?.

transcript.speaker: respondent
transcript.text: Well, to me, democracy means treating everyone equally and making sure people are getting fair pay for their work. It's also about having good public services like schools and hospitals available to everyone.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: That's an interesting view on democracy. Why do you think treating everyone equally and fair pay are important aspects for you?.

transcript.speaker: respondent
transcript.text: I think treating everyone equally is just fair, you know? People should be treated the same no matter who they are. Fair pay is important because if someone works hard, they should get a decent wage so they can support themselves and their families. It's a basic part of making sure the system works for everyone.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: That makes sense. Could you give an example where you saw fair pay play out in practice or not working as expected?.

transcript.speaker: respondent
transcript.text: Sure, I remember when teaching was a bit lower paid compared to other professions. That wasn't fair, and sometimes it lead to burnout. There are also places where people with the same skill level are paid differently based on their job titles, which can be seen as not fair. That's why fair pay is so crucial—it affects people’s well-being and the overall fairness of the system.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: I see. Could you tell me more about a specific situation where you felt the fairness of pay was not seen as important and how that made you feel?.

transcript.speaker: respondent
transcript.text: Well, when I was in business, sometimes the less experienced workers got higher pay than me with more experience and responsibilities. That didn't sit well with me because I thought pay should be based on skill and experience, not just what title you have. It felt like the system was not being fair, and it made me feel like my contributions weren't recognized. That's why we need to focus on fair pay so everyone gets what they deserve based on their work, not just their job title.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: I understand. Can you also share an example where you felt the fairness of pay was actually being upheld and that made you feel positively about the system?.

transcript.speaker: respondent
transcript.text: Oh, sure. Last year when my wife and I got their salaries increased, it really made us feel good. We were both working hard, and the increase was fair. It showed that the company recognized our efforts and our value. That made us feel like the pay system was working properly, and it’s important for people to feel appreciated and that they’re being treated fairly.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: That’s a positive example. Can you share an instance where you felt the pay system was being fair to you based on your contributions rather than your job title?.

transcript.speaker: respondent
transcript.text: Yeah, that's tough to find good examples, but I guess one could be when I was in a position where I took over a project that required special skills and knowledge. I was evaluated and rewarded with a nice raise and some extra benefits because it was clear I contributed a lot to the project’s success. That felt like fair pay based on what I did, not just what job I was doing at the time. It made me feel valued and that my contributions were recognized.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: That’s a clear example of fair pay based on contributions. Can you now share a situation where you felt the pay system was not being fair based on your contributions?

transcript.speaker: respondent
transcript.text: Oh, that’s a bit harder to give a positive example, but I had a situation with a client that started out on a lower pay scale than I expected. As the project progressed and I handled more responsibilities, I found that my pay didn't keep up with my contributions. That made me feel like my efforts were undervalued, and it’s something I’ve always strived to avoid in my work. It’s important for pay to reflect the value and contributions you bring to the table.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: I understand fully. Can you now share a situation where you felt the pay system was actually being fair to you based on your contributions rather than your job title?

transcript.speaker: respondent
transcript.text: Sure, I remember a situation where I was doing a lot of creative work for a project. The work brought in new clients and made the company a lot of money. Because of that, I was given a nice bonus. It’s clear that the bonus was not just about my job title but about the value I brought to the company through my creative contributions. That felt like a fair way to be compensated.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: That example clearly shows fair pay based on value. Can you now share a situation where you felt the pay system was not being fair to you based on your contributions rather than your job title?.

transcript.speaker: respondent
transcript.text: Sure, I guess one example could be when I was doing a lot of extra administrative work that was not part of my normal job description, but it was really important to the project’s success. The extra effort didn't result in any additional pay or recognition. That felt unfair because the contributions I was making were substantial, and they weren't reflected in my salary or benefits. It’s hard to quantify all the effort like that, but it’s something I’ve thought about and hoped to be handled better in the future.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Thank you for sharing that. It's important to reflect on how effort and success are recognized. Can you now share a situation where you felt your contributions were actually being recognized and compensated fairly based partly on contributions rather than just your job title?.

transcript.speaker: respondent
transcript.text: Yes, that’s tricky to point to a specific example, but I remember when I was doing some freelance work for a project. The client really valued the work I did, and they gave me a decent raise for my efforts. I was doing some tasks that weren't part of my normal job, but they acknowledged how much value I was bringing to the table. It felt great to see that recognition, and it’s an example of how contributions can be recognized and compensated fairly.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: That’s a good example of contributions being recognized. Can you now share a situation where you felt your contributions were not being recognized and compensated fairly, even though you knew they were important?

transcript.speaker: respondent
transcript.text: I can see how you’d want to talk about that, but it’s hard to give a positive example, so I’ll try to think of one. I remember when I was doing some work that required specialized skills, and the company didn’t fully recognize the effort and the cost of that training. It meant I was carrying a bit of an extra workload, and the compensation didn’t quite match what I felt I was contributing. It felt like the recognition wasn’t as clear as it should be, and it made me think about how we handle undervalued work in the future.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: I understand, and it’s important to address these feelings. Can you now share a situation where you felt your contributions were actually being recognized and compensated fairly, even though it felt like there should have been more recognition?

transcript.speaker: respondent
transcript.text: I’m not sure I have a perfect example of that, but I remember when I was working on a long-term project with a team. Everyone’s contributions were acknowledged, and we all got a nice bonus at the end of the project. Even though it wasn’t explicitly written, it felt like we all knew our parts were important and appreciated. The team atmosphere and the shared success made it feel like we were all fairly compensated for what we did. That’s one situation where it felt like fairness and contributions were recognized, even if it wasn’t always spelled out.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Thank you for your insights and participation in this interview. It’s been valuable to hear your perspective on democracy and fair pay. Thank you.
